correctness.rationale: PASS. Monotone positive sequence T*^n T^n has strong limit A. Unimodular eigenvectors of a contraction reduce T and have syndetic compact-torus returns; complement scalar correlation φ(n)=⟨T^n z,z⟩ has nonatomic unitary-dilation spectral measure, because mean-ergodic projections at each circle eigenvalue vanish on z. Dominated convergence in the uniformly shifted geometric-series kernel establishes uniform-block averages of |φ(n)|² tending to zero. Thus times with large correlation have upper Banach density zero and cannot contain a syndetic return set, proving δ below sqrt(||z||²+⟨Az,z⟩) impossible. Every sufficiently large block contains a small-correlation time intersecting a syndetic pure-point return set, yielding returns within d+epsilon and including δ=d via positive slack. Hence δ_*(x)² is the claimed Hilbertian seminorm on (I-P)x, nullspace PH, Lipschitz ≤√2. Explicit checks of stable, isometric, backward/forward weighted-shift and normal spectral regimes agree; no finite test is used as infinite-dimensional proof.
